entries.content_osis: <div eID="gen32607" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s">Introduction</title> <div sID="gen32608" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen32609" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen32609" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen32608" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen32610" type="x-p"/> The vision of the holy waters issuing out of the temple, and their virtue; an emblem of the power of God's grace under the Gospel, capable of healing all but the incorrigibly impenitent, represented by the marshy ground that cannot be healed, <reference osisRef="Eze.47.1-Eze.47.12">Eze 47:1-12</reference>. Also a description of the several divisions of the Holy Land indiscriminately shared betwixt Jews and proselytes; to denote that in after times the privileges now enjoyed by the Jews should be also extended to the Gentiles, <reference osisRef="Eze.47.13-Eze.47.23">Eze 47:13-23</reference>. <div eID="gen32610" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32611" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">Verse 1</hi> <div eID="gen32611" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32612" type="x-p"/> Behold, waters issued out from under the threshold - Ezekiel, after having made the whole compass of the court of the people, is brought back by the north gate into the courts of the priests; and, having reached the gate of the temple, he saw waters which had their spring under the threshold of that gate, that looked towards the east; and which passing to the south of the altar of burnt-offerings on the right of the temple, ran from the west to the east, that they might fall into the brook Kidron, and thence be carried into the Dead Sea. Literally, no such waters were ever in the temple; and because there were none, Solomon had what is called the brazen sea made, which held water for the use of the temple. It is true that the water which supplied this sea might have been brought by pipes to the place: but a fountain producing abundance of water was not there, and could not be there, on the top of such a hill; and consequently these waters, as well as those spoken of in <reference osisRef="Joe.3.18">Joe 3:18</reference>, and in <reference osisRef="Zac.14.8">Zac 14:8</reference>, are to be understood spiritually or typically; and indeed the whole complexion of the place here shows, that they are thus to be understood. Taken in this view, I shall proceed to apply the whole of this vision to the effusion of light and salvation by the outpouring of the Spirit of God under the Gospel dispensation, by which the knowledge of the true God was multiplied in the earth; and have only one previous remark to make, that the farther the waters flowed from the temple, the deeper they grew. <div eID="gen32612" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32613" type="x-p"/> With respect to the phraseology of this chapter, it may be said that St. John had it particularly in view while he wrote his celebrated description of the paradise of God, Revelation 22. The prophet may therefore be referring to the same thing which the apostle describes, viz., the grace of the Gospel, and its effects in the world.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 2</hi> <div eID="gen32613" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32614" type="x-p"/> There ran out waters - מים מפכים mayim mephaccim, the waters seem to have been at first in small quantity; for the words imply that they oozed or dropped out. They were at first so small that they came guttatim, drop by drop; but they increased so, that they became a river in which one could swim.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 3</hi> <div eID="gen32614" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32615" type="x-p"/> He measured a thousand cubits - the waters were to the Ankles; a thousand more, - the waters were to the Knees; a thousand more, - they became a River that could not be forded. The waters were risen, and they were waters to Swim in. <div eID="gen32615" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32616" type="x-p"/> I. This may be applied to the gradual discoveries of the plan of salvation, - <div eID="gen32616" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32617" type="x-p"/> 1. In the patriarchal ages. <div eID="gen32617" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32618" type="x-p"/> 2. In the giving of the law. <div eID="gen32618" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32619" type="x-p"/> 3. In the ministry of John the Baptist. And, <div eID="gen32619" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32620" type="x-p"/> 4. In the full manifestation of Christ by the communication of the Holy Ghost. <div eID="gen32620" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32621" type="x-p"/> II. This vision may be applied also to the growth of a believer in the grace and knowledge of God. There is - <div eID="gen32621" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32622" type="x-p"/> 1. The seed of the kingdom. <div eID="gen32622" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32623" type="x-p"/> 2. The blade from that seed. <div eID="gen32623" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32624" type="x-p"/> 3. The ear out of that blade. And, <div eID="gen32624" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32625" type="x-p"/> 4. The full corn in that ear. <div eID="gen32625" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32626" type="x-p"/> III. It may be applied to the discoveries a penitent believer receives of the mercy of God in his salvation. He is - <div eID="gen32626" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32627" type="x-p"/> 1. A little child, born of God, born from above, and begins to taste the bread of life, and live on the heavenly food. <div eID="gen32627" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32628" type="x-p"/> 2. He grows up and increases in stature and strength, and becomes a young man. <div eID="gen32628" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32629" type="x-p"/> 3. He becomes matured in the Divine life, and has his spiritual senses exercised so as to become a father in Christ. In other words, the grace of God appears to come drop by drop; it is given as it can be used; it is a seed of light, and multiplies itself. The penitent at first can scarcely believe the infinite goodness of his Maker; he however ventures to follow on with the conducting angel, the minister of the Gospel, in his descriptions of the plenitude of that salvation, provided in that living Temple in which alone the well-spring of life is to be found. <div eID="gen32629" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32630" type="x-p"/> 4. In thus following on to know the Lord he finds a continual increase of light and life, till at last he is carried by the streams of grace to the ocean of eternal mercy; then "Plunged in the Godhead's deepest sea, And lost in his immensity." <div eID="gen32630" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32631" type="x-p"/> IV. These waters may be considered as a type of the progress which Christianity shall make in the world. <div eID="gen32631" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32632" type="x-p"/> 1. There were only a few poor fishermen. <div eID="gen32632" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32633" type="x-p"/> 2. Afterwards many Jews. <div eID="gen32633" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32634" type="x-p"/> 3. Then the Gentiles of Asia Minor and Greece. <div eID="gen32634" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32635" type="x-p"/> 4. The continent and isles of Europe. And, <div eID="gen32635" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32636" type="x-p"/> 5. Now spreading through Africa, Asia, and America, at present these waters are no longer a river, but an immense sea; and the Gospel fishers are daily bringing multitudes of souls to Christ.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 9</hi> <div eID="gen32636" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32637" type="x-p"/> Every thing - whithersoever the rivers shall come, shall live - Life and salvation shall continually accompany the preaching of the Gospel; the death of sin being removed, the life of righteousness shall be brought in. <div eID="gen32637" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32638" type="x-p"/> There shall be a very great multitude of fish - On the above plan this must refer to genuine converts to the Christian faith; true believers, who have got life and salvation by the streams of God's grace. The apostles were fishers of men; converts were the fish caught. See below. As the waters flow into the Dead Sea, where no fish, it is said, can live, its waters must be healed, that is, made capable of preserving life; and so its nature be thus far most surprisingly altered.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 11</hi> <div eID="gen32644" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32645" type="x-p"/> The miry places - "Point out," says Calmet, "the schismatics and heretics who do not live by the Spirit of Jesus Christ, but separate from his Church; and the evil Christians who dishonor that Church, of which they are corrupt members." A description applicable to the Roman Catholic Church, that is both schismatic and heretic from the Church of Jesus Christ, which is built on the foundation of the prophets and apostles, Jesus himself being the chief corner stone; for the Church of Rome, leaving this foundation, is now built on the foundation of councils and traditions, and lying miracles; the popes in their succession being its only corner stones.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 12</hi> <div eID="gen32645" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32646" type="x-p"/> Shall grow all trees for meat, whose leaf shall not fade - A description that suits the righteous, who are still producing - <div eID="gen32646" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32647" type="x-p"/> 1. The fruits of faith. <div eID="gen32647" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32648" type="x-p"/> 2. The fruits of the Spirit. <div eID="gen32648" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32649" type="x-p"/> 3. Benevolence, mercy, charity, kindness, etc. <div eID="gen32649" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32650" type="x-p"/> The leaf thereof for medicine - See <reference osisRef="Rev.22.1-Rev.22.5">Rev 22:1-5</reference>. entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 22</hi> <div eID="gen32664" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32665" type="x-p"/> And to the strangers that sojourn - In former divisions of the land, no place was given to strangers; but in this division, (which seems to have no other reference than to the Gospel, for literally such a division never took place), the strangers are to have an inheritance; intimating the calling of the Gentiles into the Church of Christ, to an inheritance that is incorruptible, undefiled, and that fadeth not away. Glory be to God for his unspeakable gift! Amen. Amen.  <chapter eID="Ezek.47"/> <div eID="gen32665" type="x-p"/>

navigation_sections.title: Introduction
navigation_sections.content_plain: Introduction The vision of the holy waters issuing out of the temple, and their virtue; an emblem of the power of God's grace under the Gospel, capable of healing all but the incorrigibly impenitent, represented by the marshy ground that cannot be healed, Eze 47:1-12 . Also a description of the several divisions of the Holy Land indiscriminately shared betwixt Jews and proselytes; to denote that in after times the privileges now enjoyed by the Jews should be also extended to the Gentiles, Eze 47:13-23 .
